root_cause.text: The Smack LSM failed to remove the previous CIPSO DOI definition and its associated default domain mapping when a new DOI value was written to /smack/doi, leaving stale entries that prevented re-adding the same DOI later and caused the default domain map to be missing for non-ambient labels.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the old `smk_cipso_doi()` function simply called `netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_add` and `netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_map_add` without first deleting the existing DOI or map, leading to `-17` (EEXIST) on re-add. The new version explicitly removes the old DOI (`netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_del`) and its map (`netlbl_cfg_map_del`) before adding the new one, and serializes with a new mutex. The CVE description confirms that after changing the DOI, the re-add of a previously used value fails with `-17`, and the default domain mapping disappears.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added a new mutex (smk_cipso_doi_lock) to provide synchronization for CIPSO DOI operations, likely to fix a race condition.
intent_record.what: Added a new static mutex definition `smk_cipso_doi_lock` using DEFINE_MUTEX in the Smack LSM module, placed after the existing mutex definitions for net4addr locking and before the IPv6 conditional mutex.
intent_record.how: This creates a new mutex object that can be used to protect critical sections accessing shared data related to the CIPSO DOI. Without corresponding lock/unlock calls in this hunk, the immediate runtime behavior is unchanged, but it enables future synchronization for that data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change default CIPSO DOI value to unknown to fix incorrect behavior when no DOI is explicitly set.
intent_record.what: Modified the initializer of static variable `smk_cipso_doi_value` from `SMACK_CIPSO_DOI_DEFAULT` to `CIPSO_V4_DOI_UNKNOWN`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the variable now starts with a value representing an unknown CIPSO DOI instead of a default constant. This prevents the system from assuming a default DOI when none is configured, likely forcing proper DOI detection or explicit assignment.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor smk_cipso_doi to support dynamic CIPSO DOI configuration with proper locking, error propagation, and allocation flags.
intent_record.what: Changed function `smk_cipso_doi` from `static void smk_cipso_doi(void)` to `static int smk_cipso_doi(u32 ndoi, gfp_t gfp_flags)`. Added mutex lock/unlock, early return if DOI unchanged, dynamic allocation with error handling, conditional tear-down of old DOI, and return of error code.
intent_record.how: Enables runtime reconfiguration of the CIPSO DOI value. The function now returns an error code, acquires a mutex for thread safety, uses caller-provided `gfp_flags` for memory allocation, checks for redundant DOI changes, and properly cleans up previous mappings before applying new ones.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor smk_write_doi to pass DOI value directly to smk_cipso_doi and propagate errors instead of using a global variable.
intent_record.what: Removed assignment to global variable smk_cipso_doi_value and call to no-argument smk_cipso_doi(); replaced with a single call to smk_cipso_doi(u, GFP_KERNEL) and returning its result if non-zero, otherwise returning count.
intent_record.how: The DOI value is now passed directly to smk_cipso_doi instead of being stored in a global variable. Error codes from smk_cipso_doi are now propagated to the write system call, whereas previously errors were ignored and the write always returned success.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add declaration of `struct netlbl_audit nai` local variable to be used for NetLabel auditing in Smack filesystem initialization.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration `struct netlbl_audit nai;` inside the `init_smk_fs` function, immediately after the existing local variable `int rc;`.
intent_record.how: No functional change yet; this variable is declared but not used in the shown hunk. It prepares for future code that will utilize it for netlabel audit purposes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SMACK initialization to clear stale netlabel mapping and properly configure CIPSO DOI with audit context and guaranteed memory allocation.
intent_record.what: Replaced a single call to smk_cipso_doi() with three calls: smk_netlabel_audit_set(&nai), netlbl_cfg_map_del(NULL, PF_INET, NULL, NULL, &nai), and smk_cipso_doi(SMACK_CIPSO_DOI_DEFAULT, GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOFAIL). The new smk_cipso_doi call now takes explicit DOI and GFP flags.
intent_record.how: During SMACK filesystem initialization, the code now explicitly sets up audit info, deletes any existing netlabel mapping for the PF_INET domain before setting a new CIPSO DOI with a guaranteed allocation (__GFP_NOFAIL). This ensures a clean state and robust DOI creation.

relevance_review.reason: The group adds a mutex for synchronization, which does not directly address the root cause of failing to remove previous CIPSO DOI definitions and default domain mappings when a new DOI is written.

The group addresses default CIPSO DOI value when none is set, while the root cause is about failing to remove previous DOI definitions and mappings when a new DOI is written. These are distinct issues.

The refactor of smk_cipso_doi with dynamic configuration, proper locking, and error propagation directly addresses the vulnerability root cause of failing to remove previous CIPSO DOI definitions and domain mappings when a new DOI is written, thereby preventing stale entries.

The group focuses on refactoring error propagation and parameter passing in smk_write_doi, but does not address the core issue of failing to remove the previous CIPSO DOI definition and domain mapping when a new DOI is written.

Group 4 adds a local variable for NetLabel auditing, which is necessary for properly handling the removal of the old CIPSO DOI and domain mapping during DOI update, directly addressing the vulnerability's root cause.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability by fixing SMACK initialization to clear stale netlabel mappings and properly configure CIPSO DOI, which aligns with the root cause of stale DOI definitions and missing default domain mappings.

candidates.rationale: Adds a new CIPSO DOI without first removing any existing DOI definition with the same value, leaving stale entries that block re-adding the same DOI and cause inconsistent state.
Sets the new DOI value that may collide with an existing DOI definition that has not been removed, leading to failure in adding the DOI.
Attempts to delete only domain mappings but not the CIPSO DOI definition itself, so the previous DOI remains registered and prevents proper reconfiguration.
Adds a default domain mapping for the new DOI; if the old DOI is not removed, the mapping may be incomplete or conflict with the stale state, causing non-ambient labels to miss their default mapping.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement only removes domain mappings but fails to delete the previous CIPSO DOI definition itself, leaving stale entries that prevent proper reconfiguration.
Attempts to add a new CIPSO DOI without first removing any existing DOI with the same value, causing failure due to stale registration and preventing re-adding the same DOI later.
Sets the new DOI value without clearing the previous DOI definition, leaving the system with an incomplete transition and a missing default domain map for non-ambient labels.
Adds a default domain mapping for the new DOI while the old DOI remains, leading to an incomplete or conflicting mapping that causes non-ambient labels to miss their default mapping.
